snippet.title: Tenchu 2: Birth of the Stealth Assassins Rikimaru Walkthrough PS1 HD Level 1 First Mission Gameplay
snippet.description:
*The Gang of Theives* *Tenchu 2: Birth of the Stealth Assassins Rikimaru Walkthrough Part 1* - PS1 Playstation

Tenchu 2 Let's Play / Tenchu 2 Rikimaru Mission 1 / Tenchu 2 Gameplay PS1 Intro Cutscene. Full Rikimaru story; all missions gameplay walkthrough 

Hey! I'm back with PS1's Tenchu 2 walkthrough Mission 1 in HD w/ commentary! I didn't plan on making this gameplay playthrough for awhile, but I was in the mood for more PS1 Tenchu stealthy goodness, so I went ahead with it. This is Tenchu 2: Birth of the Stealth Assassins on the Playstation 1 (PS1, PSX). I recorded this with my HD PVR on my PS3 unlike last time when I recorded Tenchu 1: Stealth Assassins with Fraps on the laptop, so there won't be any worries of lag and such this time round! 

Tenchu 2: Birth Of The Stealth Assassins is a prequel to the first Tenchu: Stealth Assassins (1998), with Rikimaru and Ayame being teenagers. Plus we get to meet the ever so awesome Tatsumaru! My all time favourite Tenchu character! :D YEAH! The main villain of this game is a woman by the name of Lady Kagami, Leader of the Burning Dawn. We also meet her Four Lords - Byakko, Genbu, Seiryu, and 
Suzaku!

I skipped past the Rikimaru training level because it's no fun to watch and just got right into the actual game :) enjoy my Tenchu 2 video!

A few things I love about this game compared to Tenchu Stealth Assassins (PS1) is the deeper storyline this time around. And unlike PS2's Tenchu 3: Wrath of Heaven, all three characters storylines are apart of one story and canon to each other. Meaning to understand the full story of Tenchu 2: Birth of the Stealth Assassins you must complete the game with Rikimaru, Ayame, and Tatsumaru. 

Tenchu 2: Birth Of The Stealth Assassins intro music is soulful, sad, and stuck in my mind forever. Beautiful OST in the Tenchu game series, created by Noriyuki Asakura.

New to Tenchu 2: Birth Of The Stealth Assassins (PS1) game besides new stealth moves, swimming under water etc. is the Mission Editor mode, where you get to create your own levels, place your own enemy ninjas, traps, secret doors, and hell.. even bosses you encounter in Tenchu 2's main story mode. This Mission Editor adds countless hours to Tenchu 2 and is a feature I sorely missed in Tenchu 3: Wrath of Heaven. Though the Mission Editor is dated today and may not give you the same immersion it is still worth a few hours playing around with. 

Tenchu 2: Birth of the Stealth Assassins is one of the best games on the Playstation 1 and for good reason. If you enjoy late 90's / early 2000 era games than Tenchu 2 is the game for you.

Tenchu's Azuma Ninja have served the House of Gohda for countless generations. Now three young ninja, Tatsumaru, Rikimaru and Ayame, must protect Lord Gohda Matsunoshin against a coup d'état attempt and a mysterious ninja group calling themselves the Burning Dawn consisting of their leader, Lady Kagami, Suzaku "The Red Sparrow", Genbu "The Green Turtle", Seiryu "The Blue Dragon", and Byakko "The White Tiger", the four Lords of the Burning Dawn. To make matters worse, the recently made leader of the Azuma Ninja Tatsumaru, goes missing during a battle with Lady Kagami. 

The Tenchu series is asleep, but Fromsoftware have toyed with the idea of Rikimaru & Ayame returning for another Tenchu game. Sadly, they turned it into Sekiro instead. And while Sekiro is an amazing title, one I love... A true return of the Tenchu series is what I want most. 

A Tenchu game in today's age with the detailed level design Fromsoftware are now known for. With their continued streak of great music, bosses, and atmosphere. Tenchu today would be a mind blowing adventure. When Tenchu 2 released, the story had me sucked in. Seeing Tatsumaru go through his guilt, Rikimaru become the leader we know him as, and Ayame find her place in the world as a protector of the innocent. That was all on the Sony Playstation 1 in 2000. A Tenchu return would not only be great for fans who will buy a new title day one, but the company its self would see a big return on investment. Tenchu doesn't need a Sekiro budget. 28 levels split between 3 characters and Tenchu fans are happy, and Fromsoft would see easy profit growth for their business. But, someone at Fromsoft has to have the interest in making a new Tenchu first.

The last great Tenchu game was Tenchu Fatal Shadows (PS2). If I had known at the time it was going to be the last fully 3rd person Tenchu, i'd have shown my full support for the series and bought it. Sadly, it reviewed poorly. One I can see being called DLC to Wrath Of Heaven in today's age, but it truly is worth your time to find, or at least play on emulator. 

I'm confident Tenchu will revive someday. And you can bet i'll be here to play it. Thank you for watching my Tenchu playthrough over everyone else that put their walkthrough up. Come back for Tenchu 5 someday! 

Enjoy my Tenchu 2 walkthrough, all cutscenes on Playstation 1
